messages:
kevin: Heads up — saw a 3x tail-latency spike on prod around 03:12-03:20 UTC. p99 jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms. Correlates with heavy long-context requests (>64k tokens) and a surge in KV evictions. @sasha @aj can you take a quick look?

sasha: Yea, dashboards show evicter CPU and mutex wait rising. Traces point to evicter.run holding the lock for long periods. :eyes:

aj: Pasted a small pprof snapshot from one host during the window:
```text
pprof: goroutine profile: total 423
1 @ 0x4c2f6b 0x4c30a2 0x50f2d1 0x50f4a0 0x6b91d2 evicter.run+0x12f
   - 0x6b91d2 evicter.go:243 (evicter loop)
...
```

maria: Config note: adaptive-evict is enabled cluster-wide with threshold=0.8 and a FIFO fallback when paging starts. I'm worried the adaptive toggles are oscillating under bursty hotset shifts.

evans: Hypothesis: when adaptive flips between LRU and FIFO, reinserts create tombstone/reinsert churn for long-lived contexts, causing fragmentation and paging spikes.

kevin: I'm going to start a small canary: set eviction_policy=LRU-strict on 10% of routing keys and compare p99. deploy-bot: start canary please.

deploy-bot: canary started id=evict-test-3832104321, target=10%

sasha: Add telemetry: evicter.reinsert_count, evicter.page_faults, evicter.lock_hold_ms and sample KV entry ages. Need age histogram to validate reuse vs cold reinserts.

aj: Quick local repro I used to stress FIFO reinserts:
```bash
# simulate long contexts with interleaved key churn
python tools/kv_repro.py --clients 50 --context_len 120000 --write_ratio 0.01
```
That reproduced reinsert spikes and p99 jitter locally; FIFO showed worse tail than LRU under same workload.

maria: Heap/alloc profiles from the spike show fragmentation rising ~2x. Seeing long tombstone chains and higher RSS after sustained churn.

evans: Plan suggestion: 1) keep LRU-strict on canary for 2h, 2) deploy a reinsert-backoff heuristic (cap reinserts per-entry per-minute) on canary nodes, 3) collect pprof and the new evicter metrics. Who can own telemetry changes?

aj: I can add the counters and a small pprof tracer endpoint. Will open a PR in the next hour.

kevin: Thanks. If LRU-strict reduces p99 on canary we either tune the adaptive hysteresis or default to LRU. Also file an alert: evicter.reinsert_rate > 200/s/host.

sasha: :thumbsup: logging this as a postmortem candidate and capturing follow-ups. Assigning follow-up to @maria for fragmentation mitigation analysis.

maria: Ack. I'll collect heap diffs, compare tombstone counts, and propose lazy tombstone compaction as a remediation.

deploy-bot: canary update: canary=20% now, eviction_policy=LRU-strict for canary hosts. No errors reported during rollout.

kevin: Initial 30m signal: p99 on canary hosts down to ~150ms, baseline still ~420ms. Strong signal that eviction policy is material.

aj: PR #5242 opened: adds evicter.reinsert_count, evicter.compaction_runs, evicter.page_faults and a sampling endpoint /internal/kv/sample-ages.

evans: Will run reinsert-backoff experiment next (limit reinserts per-entry to 3/min). If that helps, adaptive policy needs to incorporate reinsertion rate and hotset dwell time before switching.

kevin: If backoff fixes it we ship backoff + make adaptive switch require sustained hotset change (min_duration=300s) before toggling. Avoid flipflop on transient bursts.

sasha: I'll create a ticket with acceptance criteria: p99 reduction >40% on affected timeframe, reinsert_rate < 50/s/host, fragmentation delta < 1.2x.

maria: I'll prototype lazy compaction and measure overhead.

kevin: Great. Thanks everyone — keep updates here. If anyone sees another tail spike, ping me and @oncall.

(reacts: :eyes: from sasha, :party: from aj)
